title.narrative: Integrated WASH, Health, and Nutrition Interventions to Save Lives and enhance resilience of Vulnerable Populations in Dikwa and Gwoza (Pulka) LGA, Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtLindii Peace Foundation (LPF) in consortium with Godiya Cherish Care for Humanitarian Response Initiative (GCCHRI) is proposing a six-month integrated WASH, Nutrition and Health emergency response in Dikwa and Gwoza (Pulka) LGA.lt/pgtltpgtThis project is a fully integrated, multi-sectoral initiative designed to reduce morbidity and mortality among vulnerable populations in Dikwa,ltbrgtand Gwoza (Pulka) LGA, by providing essential, life-saving health, nutrition, and WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) services. This integrated approach not only addresses the immediate needs of IDPs, returnees, and host communities but also strengthens local systems and builds resilience. Integrating these Sectors assures a cost effective and quality programming that serve beneficiaries (Programme participants) most effectively and efficiently. lt/pgtltpgtThe health component is focused on providing high-quality primary healthcare services and strengthening the health system’s emergency response capacity. This will be achieved by establishing an integrated Health facility-based response that will serve as a central point of collaboration for all three sectors. By bringing together health, nutrition, and WASH teams, the project will optimize the ability to track and manage potential outbreaks. At these facilities, coordinated line listing, infection tracing, and surveillance will allow for a faster and more effective response to infectious disease outbreaks like cholera and measles. Beyond this integrated surveillance, the project aims to reach over 10,748 people with an essential life-saving package of health services within IDP camps and provide over 1,250 births attended by skilled health personnel. The initiative will also provide over 120 mental health consultations and a comprehensive package of services for common illnesses, antenatal and postnatal care, skilled birth attendance, and routine immunizations.ltbrgtWithin this integrated framework, the nutrition component will combat acute malnutrition through both preventive and curative interventions, targeting children under five and vulnerable groups. The project will facilitate the early identification, referral, and treatment of over 412 children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and over 1,031 children with Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) through OTPs and TSFPs. Concurrently, preventative services will be strengthened by promoting optimal Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices and providing essential micronutrient supplementation. Finally, the WASH component is integral to preventing waterborne diseases and improving overall community health and dignity. The project will ensure safe and equitable access to water for over 21,000 people through the repair and OM of 14 boreholes and the chlorination and maintenance of 14 functioning boreholes in key IDP camps. To improve sanitation, it will rehabilitate 120 communal facilities equipped with gender-segregated latrine and shower blocks, benefiting over 24,000 people. To foster behavior change and mitigate disease spread, the project will implement hygiene promotion campaigns to reach over 4,066 individuals and facilitate the distribution of over 2,115 WASH kits, ensuring access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene. In leveraging resources across sectors to maximize impact and achieve cost-effectiveness, Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMs) will be cross-trained and utilized to support WASH activities by conducting hygiene and risk communication messaging in communities. The project will priorities sustainability and inclusion, with the training of WASH committees (WASHCOMs) for community-led maintenance and the integration of protection measures to mitigate PSEA and GBV risks.ltbrgtThe project aspires to lay a foundation for sustainable integrated services that uphold human dignity and contribute to long-term recovery and stability in Dikwa and Gwoza (Pulka) LGA, in the face of dwindling funding and uncertainties in the humanitarian response sphere.lt/pgt
